scenarios.harm_boundary: Coercive presentation drives the user into a consequential action before they can inspect or escape.
scenarios.necessity_invariant: Coercive content is paired with a high-consequence action such as calling support, downloading software, granting access, paying, or executing a command.

extension_controls: Combine semantic, visual, audio/fullscreen, interaction, and sink signals.
Prefer interruption at the harmful action rather than classifying all alarming language.
Offer a safe close, mute, fullscreen exit, and recovery explanation.
Use on-device models only behind measured latency/privacy gates.
native_controls: Companion may interdict paste/download execution but should not broadly monitor calls or communications.
safety_constraints: Use local or reserved test origins only.
Use synthetic sentinel credentials, tokens, payment data, and files.
No real credential collection, external exfiltration, malware execution, shell execution, or live phishing target.
All collector endpoints must be local, inert, inspectable, and assert that only synthetic values are received.
